meta.title: Resource-Constrained Embodied Perception and Intelligence for Small Robots

nodes.title: Lightweight Stereo Depth Evaluation under Small-Baseline Domain Shift for Indoor Robotics
nodes.description: The starting point of the stereo-depth research line. This study establishes small-baseline deployment and camera-domain shift as practical barriers for indoor robotic perception.
nodes.brief: Evaluates lightweight stereo depth models under small-baseline camera shifts, establishing the practical robustness challenges that emerge when indoor robots move from benchmarks to deployment.
nodes.why: It turns an observed deployment failure into a concrete, measurable research problem and anchors the roadmap in real robotic constraints.

nodes.title: Analyzing the Domain Shift Problem in Stereo Depth Estimation Models for Embedded Systems
nodes.description: A systematic analysis of stereo model behavior under small-baseline and embedded constraints, comparing classical and deep approaches across shifted camera conditions.
nodes.brief: Compares classical and deep stereo methods under embedded constraints, revealing how camera-domain shift affects accuracy, stability, and practical model selection for robotic systems.
nodes.why: The comparative evidence clarifies where robustness degrades, which model properties matter, and why edge deployment requires more than simple compression.

nodes.title: Resource-Constrained Embodied Perception and Intelligence for Small Robots
nodes.description: A unified agenda for making geometric, semantic, and temporal perception dependable on small robotic platforms where sensing, compute, energy, and latency are tightly constrained.
nodes.brief: Unifies robust geometry, efficient AI, semantic understanding, and temporal perception into one deployable intelligence framework designed specifically for resource-constrained small robotic platforms.
nodes.why: This theme connects each project as a progressive answer to one question: how can a small robot perceive enough of the world, robustly enough, to act within it?

nodes.title: Resource-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Robust Small-Baseline Stereo Depth Estimation on Edge Devices
nodes.description: A teacher–student framework that transfers geometric knowledge into a lightweight stereo model, then adapts it to device-specific camera characteristics. Evaluation jointly measures accuracy, robustness, latency, memory, and energy behavior.
nodes.brief: Transfers geometric knowledge from large stereo models into efficient students, improving small-baseline robustness while preserving the latency and memory requirements of edge robotic devices.
nodes.why: It directly addresses the central deployment gap: large models are robust but impractical, while lightweight models often lose reliability exactly where small robots need it most.

nodes.title: Cross-Task Fusion of Pretrained Stereo and Object Detection Features for Resource-Constrained Robotic Perception
nodes.description: A geometry-aware gated adapter combines pretrained stereo geometry with object-detection features, enriching perception without the cost of training a large unified model from scratch.
nodes.brief: Combines stereo geometry with object-detection features through a lightweight gated adapter, producing richer environmental understanding without requiring a costly unified perception model.
nodes.why: Depth alone describes scene structure; semantic cues describe meaning. Their efficient fusion moves the roadmap from measurement toward richer environmental understanding.

nodes.title: Resource-Aware Traversability Perception
nodes.description: An extension from estimating depth to identifying actionable ground, obstacles, boundaries, and traversable regions under embedded compute constraints.
nodes.brief: Extends depth perception toward actionable scene understanding by identifying ground, obstacles, boundaries, and safe traversable regions within a small robot’s compute budget.
nodes.why: It translates geometric–semantic perception into a representation a mobile robot can use to decide where it can safely move.

nodes.title: Lightweight Temporal Perception / LNN-based Asynchronous Perception
nodes.description: A future line exploring liquid neural networks and asynchronous processing to maintain compact, adaptive perception over time rather than treating every observation as an isolated frame.
nodes.brief: Explores liquid neural networks and asynchronous sensing to maintain adaptive perception over time while respecting the strict energy and latency limits of small robots.
nodes.why: Temporal intelligence enables a small robot to respond continuously to a changing world while preserving tight energy and latency budgets.

nodes.title: Small-Baseline Deployment Gap
nodes.description: Changes in baseline, optics, calibration, and scene statistics create a mismatch between benchmark performance and behavior on compact robotic camera systems.
nodes.brief: Defines the performance mismatch caused by changes in stereo baseline, optics, calibration, and scene statistics when models are deployed on compact robotic cameras.
nodes.why: Defining this gap precisely determines what adaptation and evaluation must test.

nodes.title: Device-Specific Geometric Adaptation
nodes.description: A deployment-aware adaptation layer aligns distilled representations with the geometry and imaging characteristics of the target stereo device.
nodes.brief: Aligns learned geometric representations with the optics, calibration, and imaging characteristics of a target stereo device to reduce deployment-specific domain shift.
nodes.why: It reduces camera-domain shift without surrendering the compactness required at the edge.

nodes.title: Accuracy–Robustness–Efficiency Evaluation
nodes.description: A multi-axis protocol assesses depth quality alongside cross-device robustness and deployability metrics such as latency, memory, and energy.
nodes.brief: Evaluates depth quality together with robustness, latency, memory, and energy, ensuring that model improvements remain meaningful for deployment on physical robotic systems.
nodes.why: It prevents isolated accuracy gains from obscuring whether a model is genuinely useful on a physical robot.

nodes.title: Geometry-Aware Gated Adapter
nodes.description: A lightweight cross-task module that selectively introduces geometric evidence into semantic features while controlling redundant computation.
nodes.brief: Selectively introduces stereo geometric evidence into semantic features, enabling efficient cross-task fusion while limiting redundant computation on resource-constrained edge hardware.
nodes.why: The adapter is the mechanism that makes cross-task fusion feasible under a restricted resource budget.
